brief: Capacitive trackpad driver for the Sense.CAP tile (IQS7211A).
description:
@version 0.1.0

Azoteq IQS7211A mutual-capacitance trackpad controller: up to 2-finger
absolute XY tracking, relative XY, per-channel touch status, built-in
gesture engine (tap, press-and-hold, four-way swipe), and an Alternate
Low-Power (ALP) channel for presence wake-up.

**Pre-release — the sensor surface is not yet defined.** The trackpad's
electrical geometry (Rx/Tx count and mapping, conversion cycles, ATI
targets, XY resolution) is a property of the physical electrode surface,
which does not exist yet for this tile. Until it does, this driver
deliberately does NOT overwrite the chip's memory map: it identifies the
part, clears the reset flag, and exposes the runtime + config API. The
device runs on its own factory defaults, which are not tuned for any
particular surface, so XY output is not meaningful yet. See the
`@studio unsupported` blocks below for exactly what is deferred.

What IS validated on hardware today: find, init, product/version
identification, reset acknowledge, info-flag and charging-mode reads.

Communication windows: the device only serves register data inside a
communication window. In its default streaming mode a window opens every
report cycle and the part clock-stretches a master that arrives early
(datasheet §11.9.2), so plain reads simply work. In event mode, in the
low-power modes, or with Comms Request enabled, they do not — the read
returns @ref IQS7211A_INVALID_RESPONSE (0xEEEE) instead. The driver
therefore retries every access behind an explicit comms request (write
0x00 to 0xFF, wait, retry), the same shape as the IQS323 force-comms
dance on Sense.T.C. One window serves one transaction — an I2C STOP
closes it again.

The 0xEEEE response is the sharp edge on this part: it is valid-looking
data with Comms Request, Event Mode, Manual Control and WDT bits all
set. A read-modify-write that trusts it will write those bits back and
strand the device in request-only mode — recoverable only by power
cycling the tile. Every helper here checks for it before writing.

Two communication modes:
  - **Polled mode** (default): call process() from your main loop.
    No RDY pin wiring required — this is what the current Sense.CAP
    bring-up wiring (power + I2C only) supports.
  - **RDY mode**: provide a rdy_pin in config, if a pad map ever routes
    the device's open-drain active-low RDY line to a Core pad. An EXTI
    falling-edge ISR sets a flag; process() only does I2C when set.



Datasheet: Azoteq IQS7211A, Rev v1.3, April 2025

@studio tile label=Sense.CAP icon=⬚

Driver gaps (chip capabilities not exposed by this driver):

@studio unsupported severity=common category="Trackpad geometry and cycle setup" section=config
  Total Rx/Tx counts, Rx/Tx pin mapping (0x90-0x96) and the per-cycle
  channel allocation table (0xA0-0xBB) are not exposed. These describe
  the physical electrode surface, which does not exist for Sense.CAP
  yet — the values come out of the Azoteq GUI once a real surface is
  characterised. Driver-deferred, not hardware-gated: the registers
  are reachable today through write_reg for anyone bringing up a
  prototype surface by hand.

@studio unsupported severity=common category="ATI tuning" section=config
  Trackpad and ALP ATI multipliers/dividers, targets, compensation and
  drift limits (0x30-0x3B) are not exposed as a typed API. ATI values
  are surface-specific and are produced by the GUI alongside the
  geometry above, so exposing them before a surface exists would only
  invite wrong numbers. re_ati() and reseed() ARE exposed, so a host
  can re-run auto-tuning against whatever settings the device holds.

@studio unsupported severity=advanced category="Raw per-channel trackpad data" section=runtime
  The extended 16-bit blocks holding per-channel counts (0xE0xx),
  references (0xE1xx), deltas (0xE2xx) and ATI compensation (0xE3xx)
  are not exposed. The tiles PAL does address them correctly (a reg
  above 0xFF is sent as two address bytes, MSB first), so this is
  driver-deferred; it needs the channel count, which follows from the
  surface geometry.

@studio unsupported severity=advanced category="ALP channel configuration" section=config
  ALP setup and Tx enable (0x72/0x73), ALP threshold and debounce
  (0x54/0x56), and the ALP count filter (0x70) are not exposed. The
  ALP electrode is part of the same undefined surface. ALP count, LTA
  and output status ARE readable at runtime.

@studio unsupported severity=advanced category="XY filtering and trim" section=config
  The dynamic/static IIR filter parameters (0x64-0x66), finger-split
  factor and stationary-touch threshold (0x67), and X/Y trim (0x68,
  0x69) are not exposed. All are surface-tuning parameters; deferred
  with the geometry.

@studio unsupported severity=niche category="Analog hardware settings" section=advanced
  Main oscillator selection and adjustment, calibration-capacitor
  selection (0x52), and trackpad/ALP charge-transfer frequency
  (0x58/0x59) are not exposed. These are GUI-derived analog settings
  for a specific electrode stack-up.

@studio unsupported severity=niche category="Comms-request mode selection" section=advanced
  Config bit "Comms Request EN" (0x51 bit 4) chooses whether the device
  clock-stretches a early master or requires an explicit window
  request. The driver speaks both — it retries through a comms request
  whenever a read comes back invalid — but does not expose a setter for
  the bit itself, since the automatic fallback covers both settings.

@studio unsupported severity=niche category="MCLR hardware reset / RDY interrupt" section=lifecycle
  Hardware-gated on the current bring-up wiring: the Sense.CAP tile is
  wired power + I2C only, so the device's MCLR reset pin and its RDY
  interrupt line are not reachable from the Core. Software reset and
  polled operation cover both. If a future pad map routes RDY, the
  driver already supports it — set cfg.rdy_pin. (There is no
  definitions/Sense-CAP-*.json yet; when one lands, this note should
  be re-checked against the real pad table.)

@studio unsupported severity=niche category="Tx short test" section=advanced
  The Tx short-test configuration (0x50 bit 15) is a production-line
  electrode-fault test, out of scope for a runtime driver.

studio_unsupported.brief: Total Rx/Tx counts, Rx/Tx pin mapping (0x90-0x96) and the per-cycle channel allocation table (0xA0-0xBB) are not exposed. These describe the physical electrode surface, which does not exist for Sense.CAP yet — the values come out of the Azoteq GUI once a real surface is characterised. Driver-deferred, not hardware-gated: the registers are reachable today through write_reg for anyone bringing up a prototype surface by hand.

Trackpad and ALP ATI multipliers/dividers, targets, compensation and drift limits (0x30-0x3B) are not exposed as a typed API. ATI values are surface-specific and are produced by the GUI alongside the geometry above, so exposing them before a surface exists would only invite wrong numbers. re_ati() and reseed() ARE exposed, so a host can re-run auto-tuning against whatever settings the device holds.

The extended 16-bit blocks holding per-channel counts (0xE0xx), references (0xE1xx), deltas (0xE2xx) and ATI compensation (0xE3xx) are not exposed. The tiles PAL does address them correctly (a reg above 0xFF is sent as two address bytes, MSB first), so this is driver-deferred; it needs the channel count, which follows from the surface geometry.

ALP setup and Tx enable (0x72/0x73), ALP threshold and debounce (0x54/0x56), and the ALP count filter (0x70) are not exposed. The ALP electrode is part of the same undefined surface. ALP count, LTA and output status ARE readable at runtime.

The dynamic/static IIR filter parameters (0x64-0x66), finger-split factor and stationary-touch threshold (0x67), and X/Y trim (0x68, 0x69) are not exposed. All are surface-tuning parameters; deferred with the geometry.

Main oscillator selection and adjustment, calibration-capacitor selection (0x52), and trackpad/ALP charge-transfer frequency (0x58/0x59) are not exposed. These are GUI-derived analog settings for a specific electrode stack-up.

Config bit "Comms Request EN" (0x51 bit 4) chooses whether the device clock-stretches a early master or requires an explicit window request. The driver speaks both — it retries through a comms request whenever a read comes back invalid — but does not expose a setter for the bit itself, since the automatic fallback covers both settings.

Hardware-gated on the current bring-up wiring: the Sense.CAP tile is wired power + I2C only, so the device's MCLR reset pin and its RDY interrupt line are not reachable from the Core. Software reset and polled operation cover both. If a future pad map routes RDY, the driver already supports it — set cfg.rdy_pin. (There is no definitions/Sense-CAP-*.json yet; when one lands, this note should be re-checked against the real pad table.)
The Tx short-test configuration (0x50 bit 15) is a production-line electrode-fault test, out of scope for a runtime driver.

enums.name: sense_cap_mode_t
enums.brief: Charging (power) mode — reported in Info Flags, selectable in manual control.

enums.name: sense_cap_finger_t
enums.brief: Finger slot for the absolute-XY getters.

structs.name: sense_cap_cfg_t
structs.description:
Optional init config. Pass NULL for defaults: polled mode, no callback,
and the device's own settings left exactly as they are.
Every field is opt-in — a zero field means "don't touch that register".
This matters while the sensor surface is undefined: the driver must not
impose geometry it cannot know.

fields.name: rdy_pin
fields.description: Core pad for RDY. 0 = polled mode.

fields.name: max_touches
fields.description: Max simultaneous fingers, 1 or 2. 0 = leave as-is.

fields.name: event_mode
fields.description: 1 = event mode (comms only on events), 0 = leave as-is.

params.name: instance
params.description: Device instance (only 0 exists — the address is fixed)

functions.return: 1 if a device ACKs at 0x56, 0 if not
functions.brief: Probe the bus for an IQS7211A trackpad controller.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_find

functions.signature: void tile_sense_cap_init(tiles_pal_t *hal, uint8_t instance, tile_t *tile, const sense_cap_cfg_t *cfg)
functions.brief: Initialize the trackpad controller.
functions.description:
Probes the bus, verifies the product number (763), caches the firmware
version, and acknowledges the power-on reset flag. Applies only the
optional settings supplied in @p cfg — the chip's own configuration is
otherwise left untouched, because trackpad geometry and ATI values
belong to a sensor surface that Sense.CAP does not have yet.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_init

functions.brief: Read the trackpad data block and update the cached state.
functions.description:
Call from your main loop. Reads info flags, gestures, relative XY and
both finger slots in one burst, then fires the event callback.
In RDY mode returns immediately unless the RDY line has fired.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_process

params.name: ctx
params.description: User context passed to the callback

functions.brief: Register or change the event callback.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_on_event

functions.return: Major version from register 0x01
functions.brief: Read the device's firmware major version (cached at init).
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_version_major

functions.return: Minor version from register 0x02
functions.brief: Read the device's firmware minor version (cached at init).
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_version_minor

functions.return: Raw 16-bit settings version, or 0 if the tile is not ready
functions.brief: Read the settings-version label the device was programmed with.
functions.description:
Register 0x74: high byte is the settings major version, low byte the
minor. A designer stamps this when exporting a configured firmware from
the Azoteq GUI, so the host can confirm the part carries the intended
surface configuration (datasheet §10.1.1).
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_settings_version

functions.brief: Software-reset the device.
functions.description:
The reset takes effect once the communication window closes
(datasheet §9.3.2). Blocks for the device's boot time, then clears the
reset indication. The tile returns to TILE_STATE_READY.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_reset

functions.brief: Clear the reset indication (Show Reset) flag.
functions.description:
The device sets Show Reset on every boot. Acknowledging it means a
later Show Reset tells the host the part rebooted unexpectedly — a
brown-out or a device-watchdog reset.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_ack_reset

functions.brief: Force the device into its lowest-power mode (LP2).
functions.description:
Takes manual control of mode switching. The trackpad keeps sensing at
the LP2 report rate; call wake() to hand control back to the device's
automatic mode machine. Sets TILE_STATE_SLEEPING.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_sleep

functions.brief: Return to automatic mode switching, starting in Active mode.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_wake

functions.return: Info Flags (IQS7211A_INFO_* masks)
functions.brief: Read the cached Info Flags word.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_info_flags

functions.return: Gesture bits (SENSE_CAP_GESTURE_* masks)
functions.brief: Read the cached gesture flags.
functions.description:
Gesture bits are latched by the device for one report cycle, so read
them every process() call or they are missed.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_gestures

functions.return: Finger count from the cached Info Flags
functions.brief: Number of fingers currently on the trackpad (0, 1 or 2).
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_num_fingers

functions.return: X in trackpad units (0..X resolution)
functions.brief: Absolute X coordinate of a finger.
functions.description:
Only meaningful while that slot holds a tracked finger — gate on
cycle to the next (datasheet §7.2.6), so slot 0 stays slot 0 while it
is down.

The raw register contents are returned as-is. An empty slot reads
0xFFFF in practice (observed on hardware, 2026-08-04) but the
datasheet does not document that sentinel, so gate on the finger
count rather than testing for it.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_finger_x

functions.return: Y in trackpad units (0..Y resolution)
functions.brief: Absolute Y coordinate of a finger.
functions.description: Same slot caveat as @ref tile_sense_cap_get_finger_x.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_finger_y

functions.return: Touch strength in device units
functions.brief: Touch strength of a finger — the sum of its channels' deltas.
functions.description:
Scales with the sensitivity setup, so it is a relative measure, not a
force reading. Same slot caveat as @ref tile_sense_cap_get_finger_x.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_finger_strength

functions.return: Number of channels associated with the finger
functions.brief: Contact area of a finger, in channels.
functions.description: Same slot caveat as @ref tile_sense_cap_get_finger_x.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_finger_area

functions.return: Signed X delta in trackpad units
functions.brief: Relative X movement since the previous report.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_relative_x

functions.return: Signed Y delta in trackpad units
functions.brief: Relative Y movement since the previous report.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_relative_y

functions.return: Bit n set = channel n touched
functions.brief: Read the 32-bit per-channel touch status (CH0..CH31).
functions.description:
Live read, not cached — the touch-status words sit outside the data
block that process() burst-reads. Useful when unused trackpad channels
are repurposed as discrete buttons (datasheet §10.4).
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_touch_status

functions.return: 1 if touched, 0 if not
functions.brief: Check whether a single trackpad channel reports touch.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_is_touched

functions.return: 1 if the ALP channel reports prox/touch in the cached info flags
functions.brief: Check whether the ALP channel detects presence.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_is_alp_active

functions.return: ALP count value (live read)
functions.brief: Read the raw ALP channel count.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_alp_count

functions.return: ALP LTA value (live read)
functions.brief: Read the ALP channel long-term average.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_alp_lta

functions.return: sense_cap_mode_t value from the cached info flags
functions.brief: Current charging (power) mode of the device.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_get_mode

functions.return: 1 if either the trackpad or the ALP ATI error flag is set
functions.brief: Report whether the most recent ATI run failed.
functions.description:
An ATI error means the auto-tuning could not reach its target — with
no sensor surface attached, this is the expected state.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_has_ati_error

params.name: mask
params.description: OR of SENSE_CAP_GESTURE_* bits (0 disables all gestures)

functions.brief: Set which gestures the device detects.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_enable_gestures

functions.signature: void tile_sense_cap_set_tap_timing(tile_t *tile, uint16_t tap_ms, uint16_t hold_ms)
functions.brief: Set the tap and press-and-hold timing.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_set_tap_timing

functions.signature: void tile_sense_cap_set_swipe_timing(tile_t *tile, uint16_t swipe_ms, uint16_t x_dist, uint16_t y_dist)

params.name: x_dist
params.description: X distance threshold in trackpad units

params.name: y_dist
params.description: Y distance threshold in trackpad units

functions.brief: Set the swipe timing and distance thresholds.
functions.description: A swipe must cover @p x_dist or @p y_dist trackpad units within
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_set_swipe_timing

functions.signature: void tile_sense_cap_set_report_rate(tile_t *tile, uint8_t mode, uint16_t ms)
functions.brief: Set the report rate for one charging mode.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_set_report_rate

functions.signature: void tile_sense_cap_set_mode_timeout(tile_t *tile, uint8_t mode, uint16_t seconds)

params.name: mode
params.description: Mode to set the timeout for (Active, Idle-Touch, Idle or LP1)

params.name: seconds
params.description: Timeout in seconds (0 = never time out of that mode)

functions.brief: Set the inactivity timeout that drops the device to the next mode.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_set_mode_timeout

functions.brief: Set the maximum number of simultaneous fingers tracked (1 or 2).
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_set_max_touches

functions.signature: void tile_sense_cap_set_resolution(tile_t *tile, uint16_t x_res, uint16_t y_res)
functions.brief: Set the reported XY resolution of the trackpad.
functions.description:
Absolute finger coordinates are scaled to 0..x_res and 0..y_res
(datasheet §7.4). Meaningful only once a real surface exists.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_set_resolution

functions.signature: void tile_sense_cap_set_event_mode(tile_t *tile, uint8_t enable, uint16_t events)

params.name: enable
params.description: 1 to enable event mode, 0 for streaming

functions.brief: Enable or disable event-mode communication.
functions.description:
In event mode the device only opens a communication window when an
enabled event occurs, instead of every cycle. Pair it with a RDY pin
for interrupt-driven operation; in polled mode the driver reads through
the device's clock stretching either way.

                Pass 0 to leave the current event sources alone.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_set_event_mode

functions.brief: Enable or disable the device's internal watchdog timer.
functions.description:
The device watchdog triggers a full cold boot if its main loop stalls
(datasheet §10.2). Independent of the Core's own watchdog.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_set_watchdog

functions.return: 1 if ATI completed without an error flag, 0 on error or timeout
functions.brief: Queue a re-ATI (auto-tuning) run and wait for it to finish.
functions.description:
Re-runs auto-tuning on both the trackpad and the ALP channel against
whatever settings the device currently holds, then reports whether it
converged. Run this after the sensing environment changes.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_re_ati

functions.brief: Reseed the trackpad and ALP reference values.
functions.description:
Snaps the references to the present counts, discarding any drift the
long-term average has accumulated (datasheet §5.4.3).
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_reseed

functions.return: Register value, little-endian, 0 if the tile is not ready
functions.brief: Read a raw 16-bit register.
functions.description:
The escape hatch for everything in the `@studio unsupported` list —
notably the geometry and ATI registers that a surface bring-up needs
before this driver grows a typed API for them.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_read_reg

functions.signature: void tile_sense_cap_write_reg(tile_t *tile, uint8_t reg, uint16_t value)

params.name: value
params.description: Value to write, little-endian on the wire

functions.brief: Write a raw 16-bit register.
functions.name: tile_sense_cap_write_reg
